chapter.title: Measure Before Optimising
chapter.description: Why most memoisation is wasted, and how to find the real problem.

blocks.text: React is fast. Most components render in well under a millisecond, and wrapping them in `memo` costs a comparison plus memory while saving nothing. Optimisation without measurement usually makes code harder to read and no faster.

items: Open React DevTools and switch to the Profiler tab.
Press record, perform the slow interaction, press stop.
The flamegraph shows every component that rendered and how long it took.
Turn on 'Record why each component rendered' in the settings - it names the prop or state that caused it.

blocks.text: You are looking for two things: a component that renders far more often than it should, and a component that takes a long time on a single render. They have different fixes.
For measurements in code - in tests, or reported to analytics - wrap a subtree in `<Profiler>`.
`Profiler` adds overhead, so React strips it from production builds unless you opt in with a profiling build. Use it during development and in dedicated performance tests.
Rendering is often not the bottleneck

items: A large JavaScript bundle delays the first render more than any component ever will.
Unoptimised images usually dominate real-world page load.
A slow API request cannot be memoised away.
A layout thrash - reading and writing the DOM in a loop - can be far slower than any React work.

blocks.text: Check the Network and Performance tabs before the React Profiler. If the page takes three seconds to load, no amount of `useMemo` will help.

next.title: memo and Referential Equality
next.description: How React.memo works, and the reason it so often does nothing.

blocks.text: By default, when a component re-renders, all of its children re-render too - regardless of whether their props changed. `React.memo` opts a component out of that: it re-renders only when its props actually differ.
`memo` compares each prop with `Object.is`. Primitives compare by value, but objects, arrays and functions compare by reference - and a fresh one is created on every render of the parent.

blocks.caption: memo here is pure overhead: both props differ every time.

blocks.text: This is the single most common performance mistake in React. `memo` on the child does nothing unless the parent also keeps the prop identities stable.
A cheaper option: pass children instead
A component passed as `children` is created by the grandparent, so it does not re-render when the middle component's state changes. No memoisation needed.
Moving state down, or content up, solves more re-render problems than memo does - and it leaves no maintenance burden behind.
